definitions.explanation: A small ceramic or glass bottle with a narrow neck, used for serving heated or chilled sake. A staple vessel in Japanese drinking culture.

examples.japanese: {徳利|とっくり}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦お{酒|さけ}→お酒：01045_osake⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧。
examples.english: To pour sake into a tokkuri.

examples.japanese: ⟦{熱燗|あつかん}→熱燗：27548_atsukan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{徳利|とっくり}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{頼|たの}んだ→頼む：01104_tanomu⟧。
examples.english: I ordered hot sake served in a tokkuri.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{毎晩|まいばん}→毎晩：00967_maiban⟧{徳利|とっくり}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{一本|いっぽん}→一本：08888_ippon⟧⟦{空|あ}ける→空ける：18694_akeru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{楽|たの}しみ→楽しみ：01651_tanoshimi⟧だった。
examples.english: My grandfather's nightly pleasure was finishing off one tokkuri of sake.

notes:
A traditional Japanese vessel for serving sake, typically made of ceramic (⟦{陶器|とうき}→陶器：14531_touki⟧). The classic shape has a bulbous body with a narrow neck, designed to retain heat when serving ⟦{熱燗|あつかん}→熱燗：27548_atsukan⟧ (hot sake). The standard size holds about one ⟦{合|ごう}→合：27628_gou⟧ (180 ml).

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japanese drinking etiquette, it is customary to pour for others from the {徳利|とっくり} rather than for yourself. Holding the {徳利|とっくり} with both hands when pouring shows politeness. When your companion's {猪口|ちょこ} (sake cup) is empty, it is polite to refill it.

- {徳利|とっくり}⟦{一本|いっぽん}→一本：08888_ippon⟧ — one tokkuri (of sake)

- ⟦{陶器|とうき}→陶器：14531_touki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{徳利|とっくり} — a ceramic sake bottle
